title: Figure 1. A report, a baseline, and a change are different records
claim: Four studies that followed people over time compared the growth people credited to the event with the change researchers measured. Each row keeps its own event, sample, time span, and result, and the rows are not combined.
columns: Who took part, and how many
rows: S2
Two-month prospective study; n=122 event subgroup
Growth reported on the questionnaire versus measured change in the matching areas
Generally unrelated
Does not show that growth never happens
S3
Two-wave student study; n=282 baseline; n=219 to 221 raw follow-up; n=214 to 218 full-sample analytic; 66 raw event reports; n=61 to 64 analytic event subset
Perceived PTG, perceived general growth, and measured pre-to-post change
Perceived PTG was not significantly related to the other two; perceived general growth was significantly related to measured change
Does not reach beyond the small group of students who had a trauma
S4
Stem-cell-transplant study; n=187 first; n=157 second; n=91 third
Questionnaire at follow-up versus repeated measures of the same areas
Weakly related overall; not significantly related in three of five areas
Gives no estimate for other kinds of trauma; many patients dropped out
S7
Three waves over six months; Wave 1 n=804; 32,099 daily assessments
Perceived growth versus later change in current standing and in daily ratings
Did not predict later measured change in the tested models
Does not cover longer periods or every subgroup
scope: Four prospective or measurement-burst studies published from 2009 through 2024
units: Participants, completed questionnaires, experience-sampling assessments, and direction-of-result labels
denominator: Study-specific only; the rows must not be summed: S2 n=122; S3 baseline n=282, 219 to 221 raw follow-up returns, 214 to 218 full-sample analytic comparisons, 66 raw event reports, and n=61 to 64 in trauma-subset analytic comparisons; S4 n=187 first, 157 second, and 91 third; S7 Wave 1 n=804 and 32,099 assessments
date: Sources first published online from 2009-06-08 through 2023-07-20, with S7 in a 2024 issue; observed 2026-09-05
transformation: Findings are paraphrased with study-specific direction labels; no pooling, standardization, interpolation, or cross-study ranking is performed
uncertainty: Events, samples, follow-up windows, measures, attrition, and statistical models differ across rows
limitations: The table shows selected studies and leaves others out. None of the samples represents every kind of adverse event or recovery context.
doesNotProve: The figure does not show that positive change never happens, determine whether a particular report is accurate, predict any person's recovery, or tell a reader what care to seek.
alt: A table of four studies that followed people over time. In a 2009 study of 122 students, reported growth and measured change were generally unrelated. In a later student study that began with 282 people, 219 to 221 sent back follow-up answers and 214 to 218 were analyzed. Among the 61 to 64 analyzed people who had a trauma, growth they credited to the trauma was not significantly related to measured change, while a look-back rating that did not mention the trauma was related to it. In a study of stem-cell-transplant patients, where completed questionnaires fell from 187 to 91, the two were weakly related overall and not significantly related in three of five areas. In a six-month study that began with 804 adults and collected 32,099 brief daily ratings, reported growth did not predict later change. Each study stands alone. The numbers are not added together, and none predicts one person's recovery.
